newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Gen Acc upbeat after record Q1.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Gen Acc upbeat after record Q1.

text.p: British insurer General Accident Plc said on Tuesday it intended to focus on maintaining the improvement in its underwriting performance evident in its record first quarter.
"We've seen growth in original currencies of about four percent in the quarter we've got to keep that pushing ahead," chief executive Bob Scott told Reuters.
With improvements in Europe, Australia, Canada and the U.S. the aim was to keep that growth going in the future, said Scott.

His comments came as operating profits at the composite insurer more than doubled to 114 million pounds ($184.8 million) from 55 million pounds last year, helped by a fall in weather costs in the first three months of the year.
Worldwide underwriting results improved by 50 million pounds with weather costs falling by 30 million pounds.

"The weather was better than in the previous year but I think we've had some pretty good underlying improvement and we've maintained underwriting profitability in the UK which is pretty good for effectively a winter quarter," said Scott.
Most business classes remained competitive, said Scott, but the company was implementing premium increases in personal and commercial motor classes.

"All the evidence is that private motor rates are moving up. The Automobile Association survey indicates they're definitely moving after a three or four year period when they've been in decline. Commercial motor is following a similar pattern," he said.
Elsewhere, however, rates remained pretty static.
"There are some signs on content that rate increases may be being thought about but generally the weather has been good and the homewowners account hasn't suffered unduly," said Scott.
But General Accident had seen a 50 percent increase in subsidence over the same period last year, although it was too early to say whether it was going to be as bad as it was in 1991, he said.

After absorbing the intregation costs of Provident Mutual in 1996, life profits were up 45 percent. Sales of life and pension products were up 9.5 percent overall with the profitability of new business continuing to grow.

"We're concentrating on writing profitable new business in life. Margins are under pressure in every area of the insurance bsuiness, life insurance as well, but we've got a good franchise ...we can grow strongly organically we believe," said Scott.
On pension misselling the company was not among the worst 20 offenders who reportedly have been summoned to the Treasury on Wednesday afternoon.

"We have a significant work force working on our cases and we will achieve the objectives that we have agreed with the PIA (Personal Investment Authority), but it is a very small issue for us," he said.
